question: Will the Brent crude futures price reach at least $130 per barrel in the final quarter of 2026?

calls.reasoning: Yahoo BZ=F (now apparently the Jan-27 contract after the roll) is ~$109-112 on Oct 27; the October max high is $117.42 (Oct 26). The 2026 high was ~$126 (Apr 30) at the height of the Iran war, so $130 has not printed this year. Reaching it needs ~+17% within ~9.5 weeks. With implied vol ~49%, a driftless lognormal touch probability is ~35-40%, but steep backwardation means each monthly roll of the continuous series knocks the price down, and Saudi/Turkey/Pakistan-Iran talks are a de-escalation path. Against that, Houthi strikes on Saudi pipelines and record Hormuz shipping attacks keep upside tail risk high. Market check: Kalshi WTI 'hit by Dec 31' shows ~26% for $120 and ~37% for $115 with WTI ~$101 (a near-miss contract, different benchmark; the Brent-equivalent strike is roughly WTI $116-120). Kalshi reportedly has a Brent $130 line at ~20c, but its contract terms were unverified. No Polymarket/Manifold Brent match.

Yahoo history fetched: Oct 27 O110.28 H111.92 C109.37, quote 109.43, while Trading Economics shows Brent ~$115.2 - confirms Yahoo has rolled to the backwardated next contract, so the required move is ~+19% not ~+13%, which undercuts Run 3's anchor. A search summary repeated a 'Brent $130 at 19.8c' claim, but defirate's tracker (observed Oct 27 11:00 ET) lists only WTI contracts on Kalshi and explicitly no Brent contract, so the 19.8c is likely the WTI $130 rung mislabeled; not used as an anchor.
